title: The plate-versus-film measure now reads each shot's own keys: 5 of 27 keys of s02 to s04 sit 0.06 to 0.78 over the 10.0 bar
text: p023: `npm run plates -- <shot>` rendered `KeyFilmS01`, which drew s01's keys for every shot, so the shot's key sheet never got a `measured` block (its control read `film rig as drawn -> mad 98.08` and the run ended `refused`). `KeyFilmS01` now takes the shot as a prop (`--props={"shot":...}`, `calculateMetadata` for the length), `plates-from-poses.mjs` passes it and clears `out/<shot>-key-film` first, `film_compare.film_frame` reads frames by number (padded or not), and `measure-keys.py` runs, for a shot other than s01, a control of its own: the film rig's picture of the shot's best-matching key must pass and its picture of the shot's most different other key must fail (s02-cant-build: key `stack` 7.07 against 134.92; s02-the-frame `threshold` 6.49 against 138.38; s03-scaffold `reroute` 6.72 against 143.66; s04-settle `home` 7.07 against 136.40; the bar is 10.0). s01 reads as before (its own swap control, 12 film frames byte-identical to the earlier render). `measured` is written for all four shots. Five keys fail the film measure by a hair: s02-cant-build `ready` 10.58, s02-the-frame `slump` 10.57, s03-scaffold `paper` 10.58 and `real` 10.78, s04-settle `window` 10.06 (the other 22 read 6.49 to 9.96; every worst centroid is under 1.5 px, so the joints agree; the cause is not isolated here: `ready`, `slump` and `paper` read 10.57 to 10.58 within a hundredth of each other). The README says the bar is never edited to fit a key; the keys carry `verdict: REJECTED: FILM` as measured and the shot's `plates` run exits 1. A ruling is needed on whether the bar holds for these five (isolate the difference by key, then fix the shared code) or is re-measured. Cause search, 2026-10-20 (row 9.5, nothing changed in the plates or the bar): the five are not a pose or draw-order mismatch. Every worst centroid is 0.66 px or less against the 3.6 px bar (paper: head 0.66, hand L 0.36, hand R 0.68, foot L 0.28, foot R 0.31); ready and paper are the same key drawn twice (identical joints, 31 941 px union, mad 10.58 on both) and slump reads 10.57. The excess is spread over every role, not one: against the 22 keys under the bar the five read +0.25 on main1, +0.13 main2, +0.21 shadow, +0.41 light, +0.45 skin shadow, +0.78 in pixels only the film draws (a sum of 10.52 against 8.15). It does not follow the length of the plate's role edges (mad against edge pixels, 27 keys: r = -0.15; against edge pixels per drawn pixel: r = 0.08), and about half of it is inside the figure, away from the silhouette (mad over the union eroded by two pixels: 4.6 to 5.1 on the five). It is sensitive to the resampling of the film frame: moving the film picture half a plate pixel (a bilinear blur) reads paper 7.87 and real 7.99, take 7.60 against 7.82 as drawn, so the measure carries about two to three mad of raster noise at this scale, which is the margin the five exceed the bar by (0.06 to 0.78). The bar was set from eight s01 keys (7.3 to 9.6, control 12.3); across the 35 keys now measured the range is 6.49 to 10.78. No shared code was found to fix, and the bar is not moved here: a ruling is still needed on whether the plate-versus-film measure should read both pictures at one softness (a change to `film_compare.py`, not to the bar, with its control re-run) or the five keys stay REJECTED: FILM as measured.
before: no `measured` block on any key of s02-cant-build, s02-the-frame, s03-scaffold, s04-settle
after: `measured` on 27 of 27 keys; 22 accepted, 5 REJECTED: FILM at mad 10.06 to 10.78
